A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Token Recycling and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The retained method and experiments can be matched across terminology changes and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original SpecBench and MBPP inference benchmarks, tree-structure and update-strategy experiments, and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds initialization and candidate-source ablations and an EAGLE comparison. Table 5 explicitly attributes its MT-Bench quality scores to Cai et al.; those borrowed scores are separate from the original results.

M1.justification: The adjacency matrix, hot start, BFS-like retrieval, static 80-node/six-layer tree, tree-attention verification and parallel candidate updates are retained. Algorithm 1 is unchanged apart from formatting. Appendix A.2 expands documentation of how the retained tree was constructed.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses AlpacaEval queries to construct the fixed initialization matrix and reports a GSM8K accuracy check. SpecBench and MBPP remain the principal benchmarks. The PDFs do not establish whether the GSM8K samples differ from the existing SpecBench mathematical-reasoning data.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4/Table 6 adds an evaluated EAGLE comparison on SpecBench using vicuna-7b-v1.3; v1 only cited EAGLE. The main comparison methods remain unchanged: Lade is Lookahead, AR is Vanilla, and TR is Ours.

E3.justification: New protocols include random, zero and fixed initialization controls, with the fixed matrix constructed from 100 AlpacaEval queries, and accepted-only versus all-draft updates. Memory and output-quality measures are also added. The existing main benchmark settings, including greedy decoding, batch size one, model sizes and hardware, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 expands the shuffle-based hot-start analysis into multiple initialization controls and adds an ablation isolating candidates from rejected tokens. Appendix A.6 adds a two-round token-reuse case study, while A.1 examines output fidelity. Existing tree breadth/depth, update-strategy and timing analyses are retained, with timing moved to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added floating-point discussion concerns numerical precision, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 18 shared main-comparison rows in Table 1 retain their numerical values. Tables 2–6 substantially expand the reported results: Table 4 gives SpecBench MAT of 1.63 for accepted-only updates versus 2.69 for all-draft updates, and Table 6 reports EAGLE at 2.29x versus TR at 2.03x. v1's detailed shuffle breakdown is replaced by the initialization summary in Table 3.

T1.justification: The decoding definitions, equations and algorithmic reasoning are retained. The explicit top-1/argmax equality restates the existing definition. New numerical-precision and reuse discussions provide informal explanations without introducing formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction lowers the claimed improvement across model sizes from more than 31% to more than 30%, a small quantitative qualification. The central training-free recycling contribution, approximately 2x speedup and under-2MB storage claims remain; the contribution list and conclusion still retain the 31% wording.

C2.justification: v2 adds a local-pattern explanation for candidate reuse, interprets the initialization and rejected-token ablations, and discusses finite-precision output differences. It also adds a static-tree limitation and explains the speed-versus-memory tradeoff with EAGLE. These substantially expand the mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly documents tree construction from a balanced 10-branch tree using an independent validation set and iterative node selection. Additional comparison details include the EAGLE model version and the 7B/fp16 assumptions underlying Medusa's memory figure. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for AlpacaEval and attention sinks, explicitly distinguishes Ouroboros's rejected-token reuse from candidate-token reuse, and discusses EAGLE's training and memory requirements. The broader positioning within training-free speculative decoding remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and background are condensed, terminology is standardized to TR/AR/Lade, and the author line changes. Tree attention is folded into Section 2.2, timing analysis moves to Appendix A.3, and limitations and ethics sections are added. The principal narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2–6 and revises Table 1's presentation, including shaded Medusa rows and removal of the detailed shuffle row. Timing and algorithm/tree displays are redistributed within the appendices. The document also adopts different typography, heading alignment and citation coloring; the existing plots and core diagrams are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The initialization and rejected-token controls provide more direct support for the existing design, while the EAGLE comparison clarifies its speed-memory tradeoff. Tree-construction documentation and explicit output-fidelity qualifications also help. These are useful targeted gains, although the main benchmark evidence is unchanged and the new quality check is partly borrowed and sparsely specified.
